cover: Open source licenses: what they ask of you

slides.title: Your software runs on other people's code
slides.body: A typical web app pulls in hundreds of open source packages, each with its own license terms.

slides.title: Permissive: keep the notice
slides.body: MIT and Apache 2.0 allow use in closed commercial products. The main condition is keeping the copyright notice.

slides.title: Copyleft: share alike when you distribute
slides.body: Ship software built on GPL code and you must make its source available under the same license.

slides.title: AGPL: the one to check first
slides.body: It treats network use as distribution, so modified code offered over the web must have its source available.

slides.title: Source-available isn't open source
slides.body: The Open Source Initiative doesn't recognize the SSPL as open source. Read the real terms before you rely on it.

slides.title: Keep a list, review it before a deal
slides.body: A tool-generated license inventory, a short review rule, and another check before any sale or raise.
